title: Handlebar Dash
tagline: A round digital dash on its own handlebar clamp, replacing the stock instruments.
summary: A 2.8" round colour display that reads the bike's own signals (speed, fuel, gear, indicators, warning lights) and adds its own: GPS speed and trip, clock, battery voltage, air temperature, lean angle and g-force. A standard OBD-II port and three expansion slots let it grow. First bike: the J-platform 350 with the J1D3 harness (the Meteor 350).
status: Phase 1 (learning the bike's CAN bus) is ready to build, and the display head is modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed yet): a round housing around the Waveshare 2.8" display that sits on the handlebar, Harley-style, in a cradle that clamps either side of the bike's own handlebar clamp, with an optional arc of 8 LED tell-tales above the screen. The interface box comes next.

see_sub: On the bar, Harley-style, with 8 LED tell-tales above the screen. Modelled around Waveshare's published drawing and 3D model of the 2.8" display: 102.5 mm across, 39.6 mm deep.

gallery.caption: From the rider's seat: the head sits on the bar between the cradle's clamps, the tell-tales above the screen
The tell-tales, lit: turn left, high beam, neutral, ABS, engine, low fuel, battery, turn right. Each has its own 5 mm addressable LED, so the firmware sets its colour
From the side: the head behind the bar, the cradle bolted to its back cover; turning the cradle on the bar sets the tilt (clear from 0 to 40 degrees with the default sizes)
Taken apart: the shell, the carrier (the display screws to it), the back cover, the brow with its diffusers, and the cradle with its 2 caps

head_shell.name: Shell
head_shell.what: The round housing with the thin front lip. The display slides in from the back
head_shell.material: PETG (ASA for the final part). Lip face down, no supports

head_carrier.name: Carrier
head_carrier.what: The display screws to it (4 x M2 x 6 into its own standoffs); the GPS module and the CAN board go on its back

head_cover.name: Back cover
head_cover.what: Closes the back, presses the display onto the foam ring, carries the GX12 socket and 2 M4 inserts for the cradle

head_cover_stalk.name: Back cover (stalk)
head_cover_stalk.what: As the back cover, with the GoPro-style 3-prong joint instead of the cradle's inserts
head_cover_stalk.material: PETG, 4 perimeters (the joint). Plug edge down, joint up

lip_gasket.name: Foam ring
lip_gasket.what: 0.8 mm ring between the lip and the glass. Print in TPU, or cut it from 0.8 mm closed-cell foam

head_brow.name: Tell-tale brow
head_brow.what: The arc above the screen with 8 icons, each with its own light chamber and a 5 mm LED; the GPS antenna sits under its tail
head_brow.material: Black PETG. Standing on its front face (the icons come out crisp)

telltale_diffusers.name: Diffusers
telltale_diffusers.what: 8 white squares, slid into the brow's chambers from below, behind the icons (or cut them from white translucent plastic)

gps_cap.name: GPS cap
gps_cap.what: Instead of the brow: a low cap over the GPS antenna (the tell-tales show on the screen)
gps_cap.material: PETG. Standing on its front wall

cradle.name: Cradle
cradle.what: The bridge that bolts to the back cover (2 x M4) and the upper halves of 2 bar clamps, either side of the bike's own handlebar clamp
cradle.material: PETG, 4 perimeters, 40 % infill. Bridge's back face down

cradle_cap.name: Cradle cap
cradle_cap.what: The lower half of each bar clamp, with traps for 2 M4 nuts

clamp_upper.name: Stalk clamp, upper
clamp_upper.what: Around the bar, with the 2 fingers of the joint (fits the cover's 3)

clamp_lower.name: Stalk clamp, lower
clamp_lower.what: The other half, with traps for 2 M4 nuts

head_assembled.name: Display head on the bar, assembled
head_assembled.what: The head in its cradle, with the brow and a simplified display (view only)

head_assembled_stalk.name: Display head on a stalk, assembled
head_assembled_stalk.what: The head on the GoPro-style joint (view only)
